title: Write the homes rule and re-confirm step, and seed bee's own anchors
action: Document the mechanic and apply it to bee's bundle (D2 93e1001d, D7 6a502ad0, D8 4148025d). First make the installed binary carry kfm-1..kfm-5: run `cargo build --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml` then `bee dev regen` (its onboard --apply step copies the built binary into .bee/bin) and confirm `.bee/bin/bee --help --names` lists `knowledge seed-anchors` before going on. Write one new concept docs/knowledge/areas/okf-profile/freshness-and-document-homes.md through `bee knowledge new --type <the concept type the sibling okf-profile files use> --area okf-profile` and then edit its body: (1) the document homes rule — the four kinds that live in docs/knowledge (vision, glossary, area map with boundaries and invariants, decisions, patterns) and the three that live in code (verify features and tests, generated contracts, runnable runbooks), with the sentence that every area entry anchors to at least one code file or verify feature; (2) the three fields `bee.anchors`, `bee.verified_at`, `bee.verified_commit` and the grade rule, cited from plan.md Approach by pointer, not copied, plus the one-line fact that patterns carry a date and no grade; (3) the cap re-confirm step, that unverified passes, and the `--sync-ack` escape; (4) the host steps: the binary and skills arrive through onboarding, then the owner runs `bee knowledge seed-anchors` once, and `knowledge check` prints the NOTE until that happens; (5) the pull-rate measure and what a flat rate means (the lean layer is deleted next); (6) a Pointers section naming freshness.rs, sync_door.rs, report.rs and this feature's CONTEXT.md, and its own `bee.anchors` set to those three Rust files. Link it from okf-profile/overview.md (one bullet). In okf-profile/context-and-promote.md and concept-model-and-authoring.md, change only the sentences that still describe the delivery draft and the docs/knowledge/work/ work-item location (rg `delivery` and `work/` in both) to say promote proposes area bullets and pattern candidates only and that work-item records live under docs/history/. In skills/bee-capturing/SKILL.md add, in the capture discipline, one short paragraph: when a captured behaviour change touches a file an area concept anchors, re-confirm or edit that concept (`bee knowledge confirm --id`), new area entries carry `bee.anchors`, and a bundle with no anchors is seeded once with `bee knowledge seed-anchors` — cite the new concept by path, no second copy of the rule; skills/ is hashed, so run `bee dev regen` again and include the manifest. Then run `bee knowledge seed-anchors` once over areas/ and commit the seeded frontmatter; record in the cap report how many concepts received anchors and how many got none. Three seeded concepts are rule homes with `bee.applied_at` (workflow-state/capture-queue-and-the-blocker-threshold.md, doctrine-layer/delegation-threshold.md, hook-runtime/governed-paths-and-the-intake-gate.md); their frontmatter change trips sync check (b) at cap, so cap with `--sync-ack "seed wrote bee.anchors frontmatter only; applied_at files unchanged"` — this ack is predicted here, not a deviation. Finish with `bee knowledge check` (0 OKF errors, 0 profile errors; the stale_anchor warnings it now prints are expected and are the next feature's input — quote the freshness count line in the cap), `bee knowledge index` then `index --check`, and `bee dev release-manifest --check`.
